decisions.reason: Moving the LEDs from 5V to 3.3V does not change the two OR-ed 3.3V sources, their selection behavior, or the normal and standalone source assignments.

The candidate already has a complete message-444 MODIFY that changes the LED supply and data handling, removes the obsolete level-shifter part and 5V power-switching attributes, and records indicator-brightness operation.
The candidate already has a message-444 MODIFY that adds the SK6812 LEDs to the downstream 3.3V current coverage; the monitor IC, monitored rails, position, and spare-channel count remain unchanged.
The candidate already has a message-444 MODIFY removing the LEDs from the complete powered_5v_loads list while preserving the two 5V sensors; no further boost-control change is entailed.
The LED supply-voltage change does not alter the battery connector, pinout, voltage range, placement, or connection to the AXP2101.
The DCDC1 setpoint remains 3.4V to maintain the downstream 3.3V rail after the Schottky drop; adding the LEDs as a 3.3V load does not entail a different setpoint or configuration.
The source changes LED power and logic levels but does not add, remove, or alter any main-board connector.
The source does not change any panel control, input connector, GPIO mapping, button placement, or PWRON connection.
The sensor-board input and output connector topology remains unchanged; the source does not modify any supplied connector or pinout.
The SK6812 supply and data threshold are independent of the I2C series-resistor value, placement, purpose, and population policy.
The source does not add, remove, or specify any local decoupling requirement; a changed rail load alone does not entail a decoupling-state modification.
No GPIO assignment is changed by the source. GPIO5 remains assigned to the switched 5V boost used by the 5V sensors even though the LEDs move to 3.3V.
